newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to study minister's U.S. trip -- report.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to study minister's U.S. trip -- report.

text.p: Venezuela's Congress will start investigations next week into allegations that Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar used a government jet for a family vacation to the United States, local daily El Nacional reported on Sunday.

Paulina Gamus, president of the Chamber of Deputies Controller's Committee, said it was inexcusable for anyone to use government equipment for a vacation. "Anybody who uses state property for pleasure or personal gain has committed a crime," Gamus said.
She said the facts of the case would be presented to the full committee for review on Tuesday, the newspaper reported.
Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta acknowledged on Friday he had given Matos and his family a lift to Fort Lauderdale in a state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) plane in August.
Arrieta, who was flying to Washington on government business, said: "I gladly gave the minister Matos Azocar a lift and I accept full responsibility."
El Nacional reported that the cost of the flight was estimated at $25,000.
The scandal was a severe blow to President Rafael Caldera's government which has tried hard to distance itself from the corrupt image of previous governments.
Matos and Arrieta are key members of Caldera's cabinet. Matos recently secured a $1.4 billion standby loan from the International Monetary Fund in support for his economic reform program.
